sources.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, version 6.10
sources.locator: Printed pp. 22–25, §1c through Theorem 1.32; pp. 152–155, Theorem 6.37, Remark 6.38 and Hilbert-function discussion; pp. 166–167, Propositions 7.27–7.28 and their complete proofs

read_verification.method: Full PDF downloaded and relevant complete pages extracted and inspected with PyMuPDF

contents.name: Proposition 1.24 and Corollary 1.25: primes and height-one ideals in a UFD
contents.support: A height-one prime in the polynomial UFD is principal; two coprime forms cannot both lie in one.

contents.name: Proposition 1.27 and Lemma 1.28: Gauss lemma and primitive products
contents.support: The published Gauss lemma supplies the one-variable induction step.

contents.name: Propositions 1.29–1.31: content and polynomial UFD extension
contents.support: Content factorization and primitive irreducibles establish the UFD extension used in three variables.

contents.name: Theorem 1.32: finite-variable polynomial rings over fields are UFDs
contents.support: Repairs the design's citation of a repository theorem that covers only one variable.

contents.name: Theorem 6.37: plane-curve Bézout count
contents.support: The enumerative degree product motivates the retained claim; its resultant-root multiplicity is not used as a proof of intrinsic local length.

contents.name: Remark 6.38: local quotient multiplicity
contents.support: Identifies the local quotient length at isolated intersections; the arbitrary-field residue-degree factor is supplied separately.

contents.name: Hilbert function of projective coordinate rings
contents.support: The repository's published graded-module definition covers this convention.

contents.name: Theorem 6.41: Hilbert polynomial and degree
contents.reason: The source does not prove this general scheme-theoretic theorem; this pair proves the needed zero-dimensional constant case directly from graded localization.

contents.name: Sylvester determinant definition
contents.locator: p. 166, opening of elimination-theory special case
contents.support: Determinant of the degree-bounded multiplication map with fixed ordered monomial bases.

contents.name: Proposition 7.27: affine common-root criterion with leading-coefficient boundary
contents.support: Separates the joint vanishing of the two leading coefficients from affine common roots.

contents.name: Proposition 7.28: homogeneous projective common-root criterion
contents.support: A common point of projective one-space is detected over an algebraic closure.

contents.name: General elimination-theory discussion after Proposition 7.28
contents.reason: General elimination and projection algorithms exceed the binary determinant treated here, and no claim in this pair consumes the full higher-dimensional elimination theorem.

sources.title: Andreas Gathmann, Algebraic Geometry class notes (2002 edition)
sources.locator: Printed pp. 92–97 (PDF pp. 95–100), §§6.1–6.2 through Example 6.2.3, including complete proofs of Lemma 6.1.4, Proposition 6.1.5, and Theorem 6.2.1

read_verification.method: Full PDF downloaded and relevant complete pages extracted and inspected with PyMuPDF

contents.name: Definition 6.1.1: Hilbert function
contents.support: The repository's graded-module Hilbert function specializes to these finite-dimensional field components.

contents.name: Examples 6.1.2–6.1.3: polynomial and finite-point Hilbert functions
contents.support: Degree-piece counting and stabilization are carried into the local complete-intersection example.

contents.name: Lemma 6.1.4: zero-dimensional projective schemes and eventual Hilbert value
contents.support: The proof uses a hyperplane avoiding finite support and dehomogenization; the scaffold also supplies the finite-field base-change step and handles unsaturated ideals.

contents.name: Proposition 6.1.5: general Hilbert polynomial
contents.reason: The pair needs only the constant polynomial for finite projective schemes and computes it directly; the higher-dimensional Hilbert polynomial is a separate general theory.

contents.name: Remark 6.1.6: unsaturated ideals have the same eventual Hilbert function
contents.support: The high-degree torsion argument handles a homogeneous quotient without assuming saturation.

contents.name: Definition 6.1.7 and Example 6.1.8(i): degree equals length in dimension zero
contents.support: The local formula is made explicit, including residue degrees over a nonclosed base field.

contents.name: Example 6.1.8(iii): degree of a hypersurface
contents.support: The first graded exact sequence supplies the hypersurface factor before the second one.

contents.name: Proposition 6.1.9: degree additivity for a union
contents.reason: The assigned result concerns one two-form complete intersection; additivity for arbitrary unions of equidimensional projective schemes is not consumed by its proof.

contents.name: Theorem 6.2.1: Bézout for a hypersurface section
contents.support: The graded exact-sequence difference gives the degree product, here joined to the independent local-length bridge.

contents.name: Example 6.2.2: two plane curves
contents.support: The special plane-curve form is retained for the later algebraic-variety consumer.

contents.name: Example 6.2.3: tangent intersections have larger local multiplicity
contents.support: The tangent-line conic quotient is calculated explicitly rather than inferred from a drawing.

contents.name: Lemma 10.21.2: spectrum of a product is the disjoint union of factor spectra
contents.support: The proof uses complementary idempotents and R localized at each coordinate idempotent is the corresponding factor. Induction gives the finite product; the item's scheme and stalk clauses use the declared spectrum-localization suppliers.
